automotive_autonomy.what: Vehicles, autonomy, robotics, aerospace and defense: safety-critical systems, long hardware cycles, regulation, and government customers.

subskills.name: Safety-critical systems
subskills.example: Requirements traceability and safety cases are part of the spec.

subskills.name: Autonomy & perception stack
subskills.example: Know what the perception team needs from the data pipeline.

subskills.name: Defense & government procurement
subskills.example: Understand how a program of record is won and funded.

subskills.name: Mission & operations
subskills.example: Spend time with operators; their workflow is the product.

build: Course: an intro to robotics or autonomous systems (Udacity's self-driving intro, or MIT OCW).
Follow: NHTSA and FAA rulemaking for the area you care about.
At work: get a security clearance path started early if defense is the goal.
signals: PM for the perception data platform at an AV company; labeling throughput up 3×.
Led the autonomy UX for a defense drone program of record.

fintech.what: Money products: payments, banking, lending, trading, insurance, crypto, with regulation and risk baked into every decision.

subskills.name: Payment rails & flows
subskills.example: Know how a card auth, capture, and settlement differ and what each costs.

subskills.name: Regulation, KYC & risk
subskills.example: Design the onboarding so KYC is a step, not a wall.

subskills.name: Credit & underwriting
subskills.example: Partner with risk on the decision policy and its trade-offs.

subskills.name: Fraud & disputes
subskills.example: Balance fraud loss against false declines explicitly.

subskills.name: Crypto & web3
subskills.example: Understand custody models and what regulators expect.

build: Read: 'Payments Systems in the U.S.'; Stripe and Plaid docs for the mechanics.
Course: a fintech fundamentals course (Wharton's on Coursera).
At work: shadow risk or compliance for a sprint.
signals: Owned the payments stack; auth rate up 2.1 pts, chargebacks down 30%.
Launched the lending product in 3 states with risk and compliance sign-off.

healthcare.what: Healthcare and life sciences: payers, providers, pharma, regulation, and data that is sensitive by law.

subskills.name: HIPAA & regulation
subskills.example: Classify PHI early and design consent and audit trails in.

subskills.name: Clinical & payer workflows
subskills.example: Shadow a clinic or a claims team before writing the spec.

subskills.name: Interoperability & standards
subskills.example: Know which FHIR resources your integration needs.

subskills.name: Outcomes & value-based care
subskills.example: Tie the feature to a quality measure the customer is paid on.

build: Course: a healthcare systems or health informatics intro (edX has several).
Read: 'The Innovator's Prescription'; CMS and ONC primers on interoperability.
At work: get HIPAA training and shadow a clinical or claims workflow.
signals: PM for prior-authorization automation; turnaround from 5 days to 8 hours.
Launched the FHIR API used by 30 health systems.

ecommerce_retail.what: Selling things online and in stores: catalog, search, checkout, marketplaces, and the operations behind them.

subskills.name: Checkout & conversion
subskills.example: Own the checkout funnel; every field removed is measurable.

subskills.name: Catalog, search & discovery
subskills.example: Define relevance for your shoppers and test ranking changes.

subskills.name: Marketplace dynamics
subskills.example: Balance seller tools against buyer trust; know your take rate.

subskills.name: Store & fulfilment operations
subskills.example: Spend a day in a store and a day in a fulfilment center.

build: Run a small online store (Shopify) for a month; you'll learn the whole loop.
Read: 'Platform Revolution' for marketplaces.
At work: own one funnel stage and its experiments.
signals: Owned checkout at a top-50 retailer; conversion up 9%.
Launched the seller onboarding flow; active sellers up 40%.

supply_chain.what: Moving goods: logistics, fulfilment, inventory, procurement, and the systems that run them.

subskills.name: WMS / TMS / ERP systems
subskills.example: Know the system of record for inventory and its limits.

subskills.name: Demand forecasting & inventory
subskills.example: Understand forecast error and what it costs in stock-outs.

subskills.name: Transportation & last mile
subskills.example: Optimize routes against promised delivery windows.

subskills.name: Operations floor experience
subskills.example: Work a shift; the tool has to survive gloves and noise.

build: Course: MIT's supply chain MicroMasters (free to audit).
At work: spend a week in a warehouse or with the dispatch team.
signals: PM for the routing engine; cost per delivery down 12%.
Owned inventory visibility across 40 fulfilment centers.

ads_media.what: Advertising and media: ad tech, measurement, content, streaming, creators, and the economics of attention.

subskills.name: Ad tech stack
subskills.example: Know the auction and what moves advertiser ROAS.

subskills.name: Measurement & attribution
subskills.example: Prove incrementality, not just last-click.

subskills.name: Content & creators
subskills.example: Build creator tools where the creator's revenue is the metric.

build: Read: ad tech primers from the IAB; follow privacy changes (ATT, sandbox).
At work: run a small paid campaign yourself to feel the buyer side.
signals: PM for the self-serve ads product; advertiser count up 3×.
Launched incrementality measurement adopted by top-100 advertisers.

enterprise_saas.what: Selling software to companies: admin, security, procurement, multi-tenant platforms, and long sales cycles.

subskills.name: Enterprise readiness
subskills.example: The enterprise checklist: SSO, SCIM, audit logs, roles, residency.

subskills.name: Enterprise sales cycle
subskills.example: Know the buyer, the user, and the security reviewer are different people.

subskills.name: Multi-tenant platform
subskills.example: Configurable, not customized; every customization is a tax.

subskills.name: Land & expand
subskills.example: Design for the second team's adoption, not just the first.

build: Read: 'Crossing the Chasm'; SaaStr's blog for metrics and motions.
At work: sit in on a security review and a procurement negotiation.
signals: Shipped the enterprise tier (SSO, SCIM, audit logs); unlocked 12 six-figure deals.
Owned expansion; NRR from 105% to 122%.

consumer.what: Products for millions of people: engagement, habits, community, social dynamics, and taste at scale.

subskills.name: Engagement & habit loops
subskills.example: Design the loop that brings people back without dark patterns.

subskills.name: Social & community dynamics
subskills.example: Plan moderation and abuse before the feature scales.

subskills.name: Consumer research & taste
subskills.example: Read 200 app reviews a month; ship the thing they keep asking for.

subskills.name: Games & entertainment
subskills.example: Balance retention, monetization, and fun; measure all three.

build: Ship a consumer side project and get 100 users; the feedback is brutal and fast.
Read: 'Hooked' with a critical eye; study retention curves of products you use.
signals: Grew the social feature to 5M MAU; day-30 retention up 8 pts.
PM for live ops on a top-20 mobile game.

energy_industrial.what: Energy, utilities, manufacturing, and industrial operations: physical assets, safety, long cycles, and regulation.

subskills.name: Plant & field operations
subskills.example: Products live or die by the operator on shift; go there.

subskills.name: Energy markets & grid
subskills.example: Know how your customer makes money from the grid.

subskills.name: Climate & sustainability
subskills.example: Tie the product to a measurable emissions outcome.

build: Course: an energy systems intro (MIT OCW, 'Energy 101').
At work: spend time on site with operations.
signals: PM for the asset-monitoring platform across 60 plants.
Launched the demand-response product for 200k residential batteries.

telecom.what: Carriers and connectivity: subscribers, networks, regulation, and products built on infrastructure.

subskills.name: Subscriber products & billing
subskills.example: Know the billing system constraints before designing a plan.

subskills.name: Network services
subskills.example: Understand which network capabilities enable which products.

build: Course: a telecom fundamentals or 5G intro.
At work: shadow network operations and the billing team.
signals: PM for the 5G home internet product; 400k subscribers in year one.

developer_tools.what: Products for developers: tools, infrastructure, open source, and the very particular way developers adopt things.

subskills.name: Developer adoption & DX
subskills.example: Developers adopt by trying; make the first 10 minutes perfect.

subskills.name: Open source & community
subskills.example: Decide what's open, what's paid, and how the community is treated.

subskills.name: Infrastructure products
subskills.example: Reliability and pricing are the product.

subskills.name: Bottom-up / PLG for devs
subskills.example: Free tier to paid: find the usage threshold where value is obvious.

build: Use and contribute to open-source tools; write docs for one.
Read: 'The Developer's Guide to Content Creation'; Stripe/Vercel docs as benchmarks.
At work: run developer interviews and watch them use the quick start.
signals: PM for the CLI and SDKs; time-to-first-deploy from 40 to 6 minutes.
Grew the open-source project from 2k to 20k stars with a community program.

public_sector.what: Regulated and government contexts: compliance, policy, audits, procurement, and change that moves slowly on purpose.

subskills.name: Regulatory change management
subskills.example: Track the rule, map it to features, and ship before the deadline.

subskills.name: Audits & controls
subskills.example: Design for the auditor: logs, evidence, and sign-offs.

subskills.name: Government procurement
subskills.example: Know the contract vehicles your buyers can use.

build: Course: an intro to regulatory affairs or public policy for your industry.
At work: partner with legal and compliance on one regulatory project end to end.
signals: Delivered the GDPR program across 5 products on deadline.
Achieved FedRAMP Moderate authorization for the platform.

yoe_2.what: Entry-level: internships, rotational programs, and first PM roles ask for up to two years of related experience.
build: Internships, APM programs, and adjacent roles (analyst, support, engineering) all count.
A shipped side project with users is the strongest substitute.
signals: 2 years as a data analyst supporting the product team.

yoe_3.what: Early-career: three to four years, usually with at least one full product cycle owned.
build: Own one feature end to end and be able to tell its story with numbers.
signals: 3 years of product management across two B2B products.

yoe_5.what: Mid-career: five to six years, the standard ask for a Senior PM.
build: Multiple launches, measurable impact, and cross-team leadership examples.
signals: 5+ years in product management, including 2 years leading a platform area.

yoe_8.what: Experienced: seven to nine years, typical for staff, principal, group, and many director roles.
build: Evidence of strategy ownership and of growing others.
signals: 8 years of product experience, last 3 as Group PM over 3 squads.

yoe_10.what: Senior leadership: ten or more years, usually director and above.
build: Org-level results, hiring and leveling, and P&L or budget ownership.
signals: 12 years in product, including 5 leading teams of 10+ PMs.

pm_experience.what: Prior product-management experience specifically, as opposed to adjacent roles.
build: If you don't have the title yet: APM programs, internal transfers, or a hybrid role (TPM, analyst, founder) where you owned product decisions.
Document the product decisions you made in your current role; that's PM experience in all but name.
signals: 4 years as a Product Manager at two companies; owned roadmap, specs, and launches.

bachelors.what: A bachelor's degree, often 'or equivalent practical experience'.
build: Most postings accept equivalent experience; make the equivalence explicit on your resume.
signals: B.A. Economics, University of X.

masters_mba.what: An MBA or master's, preferred more often than required, and more common in strategy-heavy and enterprise roles.
build: Worth it mainly for a career pivot or a specific network; part-time and online options are increasingly accepted.
signals: MBA, with a concentration in technology strategy.

phd.what: A PhD or research background, asked for in AI research-adjacent product roles.
build: Relevant mainly for research-lab product roles; a strong publication record or research engineering experience is the practical substitute.
signals: PhD in Computer Science (NLP); 3 publications.

cs_engineering_degree.what: A computer science or engineering degree, or an engineering background, asked for by technical PM and TPM roles.
build: Without the degree: a software engineering stint, a bootcamp plus shipped code, or a technical certification plus evidence you read and discuss code.
signals: B.S. Computer Science; 2 years as a backend engineer before moving to product.

startup_experience.what: Having worked at an early-stage or high-growth company, as evidence you can operate with little structure.
build: Join one, found one, or do a meaningful project with one; hackathons and accelerators count at the margin.
signals: Employee #8 at a seed-stage fintech; built the product function through Series A.

big_tech_experience.what: Experience at scale: products with millions of users or large organizations.
build: A role at a large platform, or ownership of a high-traffic surface anywhere.
signals: PM at a top-5 tech company on a surface with 50M MAU.

consulting_banking.what: A consulting, banking, or strategy background, valued for structured thinking and executive communication.
build: Not required; the transferable parts are structured problem solving and business cases, both of which you can show directly.
signals: 2 years at a strategy consultancy before product.

security_clearance.what: A security clearance or U.S. person status, required for defense and some government work.
build: Clearances are sponsored by employers; being clearable (citizenship, clean record) is what you can control.
signals: Active Secret clearance.
